member: Tomas - Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Analyst
message:
Elena, Marcus, Priya, comfort is judged by maximum below 0.5 and minimum below 1.0 metres per second squared, with the 1.9 Hz mode inside the resonant range, in the Experimental and Numerical Study on Dynamics of Two Footbridges (E38). In plain words the bridge must stay under gentle braking feel, then the numbers that decide are 0.500 metres per second squared for maximum and 1.00 metres per second squared for minimum.

Elena, Marcus, Priya, the dense crowd pushes the bare bridge to almost lifting people while the hidden damper brings it to gentle bus braking, checked against body weight and gravity. In plain words uncontrolled is violent and controlled is comfortable, then the numbers that decide are the dense-crowd resonant force estimate (E50) of 1.48e3 N giving the bare-deck acceleration scaling (E51) of 9.26 metres per second squared, 0.944 times gravity and outside footbridge experience because linear resonance overpredicts, versus the Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, secondary mass tuned to the bridge mode) controlled acceleration scaling (E52) of 0.545 metres per second squared, 0.0556 times gravity.

Elena, Marcus, Priya, the moving mass stays clear of its stops with thumbnail motion. In plain words no impact jolts, then the numbers that decide are the dense-crowd stroke scaling (E53) of 20.1 mm with 2.49 times margin to plus-minus 50 mm stops in the bolted frame sketch (E37). Not ready, because the integrated proposal is still missing.
